title: Zephaniah 1 — The great day of YHWH is near

verdicts.reasoning: dəḇar-YHWH ʾăšer hāyâ ʾel-ṣəp̄anyâ ben-kûšî ...: English name forms and exact genealogy.
ʾāsōp̄ ʾāsēp̄ kōl (inf. abs. of ʾsp + Hiphil of swp): ASV 'utterly consume' renders the sense, and the two-root play is explained in commentary. Exact.

ʾāsēp̄ ʾāḏām ûḇəhēmâ ... wəhammaḵšēlôṯ ʾeṯ-hārəšāʿîm ...: the MT 'stumbling blocks' is kept with NRSV's emendation reported. 'human ... the human' keeps the ʾāḏām/ʾăḏāmâ play of Gen 2:7 under central adam-adamah. Exact.
šəʾār habbaʿal ʾeṯ-šēm hakkəmārîm ʿim-hakkōhănîm: 'the Chemarim' (ASV) as a technical term with gloss. Exact.

liṣḇāʾ haššāmayim ... wəhannišbāʿîm bəmalkām: 'host of the heavens' applies the ratified divine-realm register (central tzeva-ha-shamayim). The ASV 'Malcam' leaves MT 'their king' against versional Milcom undecided. Exact.
hannəsôḡîm mēʾaḥărê YHWH ... wəlōʾ ḏərāšuhû: exact.
has mippənê ʾăḏōnāy YHWH ... hēḵîn YHWH zeḇaḥ hiqdîš qərūʾāyw: exact.

Disputed: śārîm 'officials' against ASV 'princes'. śar is the general term for an official (BDB, HALOT), and NRSV and NJPS print 'officials'; the ezekiel-woh ruling is followed. The Isaiah divergence is F2.

citations: Roberts, Nahum, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah (OTL, 1991), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: kol-haddôlēḡ ʿal-hammip̄tān ... bêṯ ʾăḏōnêhem ḥāmās ûmirmâ: ASV, with the 1 Sam 5:5 custom and the 'dais' alternative in commentary. Exact.

Disputed only typographically: šaʿar haddāḡîm 'the Fish Gate' and hammišneh 'the Second Quarter' as capitalized names, as NRSV does; the gate is named at Neh 3:3. The reception note matches TBWTT ch. 5 ('There shall be in that day a loud clamor from the side of the Fish Gate') and is labelled; the capital marks a toponym and carries no age-of-Pisces reading.

Disputed: 'the Mortar' for hammaḵtēš (NRSV) and 'the merchant people' for ʿam kənaʿan. kənaʿan 'trader' is lexically secured (Hos 12:8; Prov 31:24); KJV's text and the ASV margin have 'merchant people', and the parallel 'laden with silver' confirms the sense.
ʾăḥappēś ʾeṯ-yərûšālaim bannērôṯ ... haqqōp̄əʾîm ʿal-šimrêhem ...: exact, and the quoted words keep their marks under the convention.

Re-checked the accents: ʾaṯnaḥ on məʾōḏ and zaqef on YHWH in qôl yôm YHWH, so the MT division 'the sound of the day of YHWH; the mighty man cries out there bitterly' (ASV) is followed correctly, with the NRSV joining of mar reported.
yôm ʿeḇrâ ... ṣārâ ûməṣûqâ ... šōʾâ ûməšôʾâ ... ʿānān waʿărāp̄el: exact; central tzarah and arafel applied.
Disputed: 'shofar' against ASV 'trumpet'. šôp̄ār is the ram's horn, distinct from the ḥăṣōṣərâ, and the corpus already transliterates it in Exodus and Kings. The Isaiah 27:13 divergence is F2.
wahăṣērōṯî lāʾāḏām ... ûləḥumām kaggəlālîm: 'men' for generic ʾāḏām and 'flesh' for the rare ləḥûm are defensible. Exact.

Disputed: kol-hāʾāreṣ 'the whole earth' against ASV/NJPS 'land'. Tested at the editor's request. The universal frame of vv2-3 (humans, beasts, birds and fish 'from the face of the ground') and the recurrence of the phrase at 3:8 in a judgment on all nations support NRSV's 'earth'. The scope test is applied as stated in the overlay, and both readings are in commentary.

glossaryReview.reasoning: direct is right for a presentation convention with no interpretive content. Verified in the lines: English names, 'the Lord YHWH' / 'the Lord', unquoted messenger formula (Jer 10:2, 18), quoted speech inside oracles and visions, and nəʾum 'declares' kept distinct from ʾāmar 'says' (Zech 4:6 against 5:4). Two open points are recorded under founder recommendations: F3, where the reviewer supports 'declares', and F4, where the reviewer supports ratification. Text identical in all five overlays (hash-checked).
Approve: the MT/ASV is kept at all six sites, the accent division at 1:14 was verified in the source, and the alternatives are reported.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012)

glossaryReview.reasoning: Verified against the source: the three bracketed Ketiv/Qere pairs are Jer 10:13 (article), Jer 10:17 (archaic -tî) and Zech 4:2 (wyʾmr/wāʾōmar, sense-changing), and the Qere is translated at each. The versional readings listed are reported and not adopted, and the rafe at Zech 5:11 is handled correctly. direct is right for a textual policy consistent with the corpus.
Approve: 'officials' matches the general sense of śar and ezekiel-woh 11:1 ('officials of the people', checked). The Isaiah 'princes' divergence is F2.

Approve. Rendering the three Jerusalem districts uniformly as English names (NRSV 'Fish Gate', 'Second Quarter', 'Mortar') is consistent. kənaʿan 'trader' is lexically secured, and 'merchant people' is the KJV text and the ASV margin. The entry explicitly keeps the canon's Pisces/Aquarius reading out of the capital.
Approve: the šôp̄ār is distinct from the ḥăṣōṣərâ, and transliteration is corpus practice in Exodus and Kings. The Isaiah 27:13 divergence is F2.

direct is defensible because the scope test is applied from markers inside each verse: tēḇēl/šāmayim pairing, ʾăḏôn kol-hāʾāreṣ, ʾap̄sê-ʾāreṣ, 2 Chr 16:9. Every 'earth' site matches ASV or NRSV, and 'land' is kept for territory. Zeph 1:18 was tested and approved, with NRSV against ASV/NJPS, both in commentary.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 18 lines in the English alone. No English line reads as interpretation. The canon-cited verses (1:10) render the Hebrew at standard values, and each reception note is under its own 'Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim)' heading. Each note's quotation was verified against the canon text (TBWTT ch. 3 and ch. 5, FR/EN). Capitalisation (e.g. 'the Fish Gate') and vocabulary updates ('scroll', 'lampstand') are register or name conventions with lexical basis, not lens.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 109 LP1 lines, 31 overlay entries and 27 central ops were formed from the chapters, the sources, the drafts, the overlays and the diff, and recorded before wave-lp1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's watch points were each re-tested: Zeph 1:18 'earth', Zeph 1:10-11 names, Zech 4:14, Zech 9:9, Jer 10:5 and the unquoted Jer 10:2-5. The report does not mention the two Zech 4 speech-line issues (4:10 quote boundary; 4:13 'answered'), which stand as revise. The founder points F1-F5 are answered below.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-isaiah-aligned-conventions: Ratify for the Latter Prophets: 'God', 'earth'/'land' by scope, lowercase 'spirit', 'create' and 'oracle' are each the ASV/NRSV/NJPS-backed rendering and keep the five books one volume with Isaiah. Harmonize Ezekiel at its next wave, not by retro-editing signed-off chapters. The 'God'/'Elohim' split is the one item the reviewer flags for explicit founder ratification, because it is a project-stance choice.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-officials-shofar-vs-isaiah: Align Isaiah to 'officials' (Isa 32:1; 40:23; 43:28) and 'shofar' (Isa 27:13) at its next pass; both are lexically better grounded and already corpus rulings. Then promote megillah/menorah/sarim/shofar to central entries as the report proposes. Keep the Exodus 25 'lampstand' dependency on the Exodus checklist.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-neum-declares: Adopt 'declares YHWH' corpus-wide. Zechariah has ʾāmar YHWH (4:6) and nəʾum YHWH (5:4) within a few verses, and Isaiah's 'says' for both (e.g. ISA-14:22, checked) erases a distinction the Hebrew makes. Align Isaiah later.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-unquoted-messenger-formula: Ratify. At Jer 10:2-6 the Hebrew does not mark where the oracle ends, and leaving it unquoted avoids inventing a boundary. Related: at Zech 4:9-10 the wave's own marks run YHWH's word into the messenger's answer, which is the reviewer's revise at ZEC-WOH-4:10.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-sons-of-fresh-oil: Ship 'the two sons of fresh oil'. It is the most literal rendering, lexically grounded (yiṣhār, no māšaḥ), and inferred is the honest label; 'anointed ones' stays in commentary for reception continuity. If the founder wants a gentler line, 'the two sons of oil' (ASV margin) is the conservative literal fallback.

paragraphs.text: דְּבַר־יְהוָ֣ה ׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֗ה אֶל־צְפַנְיָה֙ בֶּן־כּוּשִׁ֣י בֶן־גְּדַלְיָ֔ה בֶּן־אֲמַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן־חִזְקִיָּ֑ה בִּימֵ֛י יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בֶן־אָמ֖וֹן מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: The word of YHWH that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.

notes.official: *dəḇar-YHWH ʾăšer hāyâ ʾel-ṣəp̄anyâ* 'The word of YHWH that came to Zephaniah' (central `davar-yhwh-prophetic-formula`). The four-generation genealogy is unusually long and reaches back to a Hezekiah, perhaps the king (Berlin, *Zephaniah*, AB 25A, 1994). *ben-kûšî* 'son of Cushi': *kûšî* is a personal name here (as Jer 36:14), though the word also means 'the Cushite'. English name forms throughout (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`). The setting is the reign of Josiah (640-609 BCE), before or during his reform (2 Kgs 22-23).

paragraphs.text: אָסֹ֨ף אָסֵ֜ף כֹּ֗ל מֵעַ֛ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: I will utterly consume all things from off the face of the ground, declares YHWH.

notes.official: *ʾāsōp̄ ʾāsēp̄ kōl* 'I will utterly consume all things': the infinitive is from *ʾsp* 'gather' and the finite verb is a Hiphil of *swp* 'make an end' (cf. Jer 8:13). No English verb reproduces the play of two roots, and the ASV's 'utterly consume' renders the sense (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zephaniah-1`; NRSV 'utterly sweep away'). *mēʿal pənê hāʾăḏāmâ* 'from off the face of the ground' (central `adam-adamah`).

paragraphs.text: אָסֵ֨ף אָדָ֜ם וּבְהֵמָ֗ה אָסֵ֤ף עוֹף־הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וּדְגֵ֣י הַיָּ֔ם וְהַמַּכְשֵׁל֖וֹת אֶת־הָרְשָׁעִ֑ים וְהִכְרַתִּ֣י אֶת־הָאָדָ֗ם מֵעַ֛ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: I will consume human and beast; I will consume the birds of the skies and the fish of the sea, and the stumbling blocks with the wicked; and I will cut off the human from off the face of the ground, declares YHWH.

notes.official: The list *ʾāḏām ûḇəhēmâ ... ʿôp̄-haššāmayim ûḏəḡê hayyām* 'human and beast ... the birds of the skies and the fish of the sea' runs the creation of Gen 1 backwards, from the last created to the first, and *ʾāḏām* / *hāʾăḏāmâ* repeat the wordplay of Gen 2:7 (central `adam-adamah`, `shamayim`; Berlin, AB 25A; Sweeney, *Zephaniah*, Hermeneia, 2003). *wəhammaḵšēlôṯ ʾeṯ-hārəšāʿîm* 'and the stumbling blocks with the wicked' is obscure; the stumbling blocks may be idols (Ezek 14:3-7), and NRSV emends to *wəhiḵšaltî* 'I will make the wicked stumble'. The MT is kept (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zephaniah-1`; `mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וְנָטִ֤יתִי יָדִי֙ עַל־יְהוּדָ֔ה וְעַ֖ל כָּל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֞י מִן־הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֶת־שְׁאָ֣ר הַבַּ֔עַל אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם הַכְּמָרִ֖ים עִם־הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃

i18n.en: And I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, the name of the Chemarim with the priests,

notes.official: *šəʾār habbaʿal* 'the remnant of Baal': the article on the divine name is idiomatic and is not rendered, following English usage (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`). *šēm hakkəmārîm ʿim-hakkōhănîm* 'the name of the Chemarim with the priests': *kəmārîm* is an Aramaic loan for the priests of foreign cults (2 Kgs 23:5; Hos 10:5; NRSV 'the idolatrous priests'), kept in the ASV's transliteration as a technical term (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zephaniah-1`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁתַּחֲוִ֥ים עַל־הַגַּגּ֖וֹת לִצְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְאֶת־הַמִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוִים֙ הַנִּשְׁבָּעִ֣ים לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהַנִּשְׁבָּעִ֖ים בְּמַלְכָּֽם׃

i18n.en: and those who worship the host of the heavens on the housetops, and those who worship, who swear to YHWH and swear by Malcam,

notes.official: *hammištaḥăwîm ʿal-haggaggôṯ liṣḇāʾ haššāmayim* 'those who worship the host of the heavens on the housetops': the astral cult of the late monarchy (2 Kgs 21:3-5; 23:5, 12; Jer 19:13), rendered with 'heavens' by the central entry (central `tzeva-ha-shamayim-host-of-the-heavens-divine-council-cross-corpus`). 'Worship' (ASV) translates *hištaḥăwâ* in its cultic sense; the central entry for the homage of the Joseph cycle ('made obeisance') does not apply. *bəmalkām*: the MT vowels give 'by their king', and the versions read Milcom, the Ammonite god (1 Kgs 11:5, 33; Vulgate; NRSV). The line keeps the ASV's 'Malcam', which keeps the consonants without deciding (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zephaniah-1`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־הַנְּסוֹגִ֖ים מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַאֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־בִקְשׁ֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א דְרָשֻֽׁהוּ׃

i18n.en: and those who have turned back from following YHWH, and who have not sought YHWH nor inquired of him.

paragraphs.text: הַ֕ס מִפְּנֵ֖י אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה כִּ֤י קָרוֹב֙ י֣וֹם יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־הֵכִ֧ין יְהוָ֛ה זֶ֖בַח הִקְדִּ֥ישׁ קְרֻאָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Be silent before the Lord YHWH! For the day of YHWH is near; for YHWH has prepared a sacrifice, he has consecrated his guests.

notes.official: *has* 'Be silent!' before the Lord YHWH (central `adonai-yhwh`; cf. Hab 2:20; Zech 2:17). *kî-hēḵîn YHWH zeḇaḥ hiqdîš qərūʾāyw* 'for YHWH has prepared a sacrifice, he has consecrated his guests' (*zeḇaḥ* 'sacrifice', central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`): the day of YHWH as a sacrificial feast, with Judah as the victim and the invited guests as the executioners (cf. Isa 34:6; Jer 46:10; Ezek 39:17-20).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּיוֹם֙ זֶ֣בַח יְהוָ֔ה וּפָקַדְתִּ֥י עַל־הַשָּׂרִ֖ים וְעַל־בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־הַלֹּבְשִׁ֖ים מַלְבּ֥וּשׁ נָכְרִֽי׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass on the day of YHWH's sacrifice that I will punish the officials and the king's sons, and all who are clothed in foreign apparel.

notes.official: *ûp̄āqaḏtî ʿal-haśśārîm* 'I will punish the officials': the *śārîm* are the court officials, named beside 'the king's sons', the princes of the royal house. 'Officials' (NRSV, NJPS) replaces the draft's ASV 'princes' under the corpus ruling for *śar* (`sarim-officials-latter-prophets`; ezekiel-woh 11:1); isaiah-woh still has 'princes' (Isa 32:1; 43:28), a divergence flagged for the founder. *malbûš noḵrî* 'foreign apparel', the dress of a foreign court or cult. *zeḇaḥ YHWH* 'YHWH's sacrifice' (central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וּפָקַדְתִּ֗י עַ֧ל כָּל־הַדּוֹלֵ֛ג עַל־הַמִּפְתָּ֖ן בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא הַֽמְמַלְאִ֛ים בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנֵיהֶ֖ם חָמָ֥ס וּמִרְמָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And on that day I will punish everyone who leaps over the threshold, who fill their master's house with violence and deceit.

notes.official: *kol-haddôlēḡ ʿal-hammip̄tān* 'everyone who leaps over the threshold' (central `mifthan-ha-bayit`): probably the custom of avoiding the threshold known from the Philistine temple of Dagon (1 Sam 5:5), here adopted at court. Some take *mip̄tān* as the throne-podium and render 'who mounts the dais' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zephaniah-1`; Roberts, *Nahum, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah*, OTL, 1991). *bêṯ ʾăḏōnêhem* 'their master's house': the plural *ʾăḏōnîm* is a plural of majesty, for the king or for the deity whose house it is.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה ק֤וֹל צְעָקָה֙ מִשַּׁ֣עַר הַדָּגִ֔ים וִֽילָלָ֖ה מִן־הַמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּד֖וֹל מֵהַגְּבָעֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass on that day, declares YHWH, that there shall be the sound of a cry from the Fish Gate, and a wailing from the Second Quarter, and a great crash from the hills.

notes.official:
*qôl ṣəʿāqâ miššaʿar haddāḡîm* 'the sound of a cry from the Fish Gate': the Fish Gate was a gate in the north wall of Jerusalem (Neh 3:3; 12:39; 2 Chr 33:14), probably named after the fish market supplied by Tyrian traders (Neh 13:16). *hammišneh* 'the Second Quarter' is the newer western district where Huldah lived (2 Kgs 22:14). The line renders both as English names with capitals, as NRSV does, under the shared name convention; this replaces the draft's lower-case forms (overlay `fish-gate-mishneh-maktesh-zephaniah-1-10-11`). *šeḇer gāḏôl mēhaggəḇāʿôṯ* 'a great crash from the hills'. *nəʾum-YHWH* 'declares YHWH' (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 5) quotes the first half of the verse ('There shall be in that day a loud clamor from the side of the Fish Gate') and reads the Fish Gate as the passage from the age of Pisces into the age of Aquarius, the clamor being the noise of the revelation. The line renders *šaʿar haddāḡîm* as the name of a Jerusalem gate; the capital marks a place-name and nothing more.

paragraphs.text: הֵילִ֖ילוּ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הַמַּכְתֵּ֑שׁ כִּ֤י נִדְמָה֙ כָּל־עַ֣ם כְּנַ֔עַן נִכְרְת֖וּ כָּל־נְטִ֥ילֵי כָֽסֶף׃

i18n.en: Wail, you inhabitants of the Mortar, for all the merchant people are undone; all who were laden with silver are cut off.

notes.official: *hêlîlû yōšəḇê hammaḵtēš* 'Wail, you inhabitants of the Mortar': *maḵtēš* 'mortar, hollow' names a low-lying market district (Berlin, AB 25A; Sweeney, Hermeneia). It is rendered as an English name like the Fish Gate and the Second Quarter (NRSV), in place of the ASV's transliteration 'Maktesh'. *kol-ʿam kənaʿan* 'all the merchant people': *kənaʿan* is here the common noun 'trader' (Hos 12:8; Isa 23:8; Prov 31:24), as the parallel 'all who were laden with silver' shows. The ASV text has 'the people of Canaan' and its margin 'merchant people', which the line adopts (NRSV 'the traders'; overlay `fish-gate-mishneh-maktesh-zephaniah-1-10-11`). *nidmâ* 'are undone' (cf. Isa 6:5).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא אֲחַפֵּ֥שׂ אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּנֵּר֑וֹת וּפָקַדְתִּ֣י עַל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַקֹּֽפְאִים֙ עַל־שִׁמְרֵיהֶ֔ם הָאֹֽמְרִים֙ בִּלְבָבָ֔ם לֹֽא־יֵיטִ֥יב יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יָרֵֽעַ׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass at that time that I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish the men who are settled on their lees, who say in their heart, "YHWH will not do good, nor will he do evil."

notes.official: *ʾăḥappēś ʾeṯ-yərûšālaim bannērôṯ* 'I will search Jerusalem with lamps'. *haqqōp̄əʾîm ʿal-šimrêhem* 'who are settled on their lees': wine left on its sediment thickens (Jer 48:11), an image of complacency. Their words are quoted inside the oracle and keep their marks (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`): YHWH 'will not do good, nor will he do evil', that is, he does nothing at all.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה חֵילָם֙ לִמְשִׁסָּ֔ה וּבָתֵּיהֶ֖ם לִשְׁמָמָ֑ה וּבָנ֤וּ בָתִּים֙ וְלֹ֣א יֵשֵׁ֔בוּ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁתּ֖וּ אֶת־יֵינָֽם׃

i18n.en: And their wealth shall become a spoil, and their houses a desolation; they shall build houses but not inhabit them, and they shall plant vineyards but not drink their wine.

notes.official: The futility curse of Deut 28:30, 39: houses not lived in, vineyards whose wine is not drunk (central `kerem-vineyard`).

paragraphs.text: קָר֤וֹב יוֹם־יְהוָה֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל קָר֖וֹב וּמַהֵ֣ר מְאֹ֑ד ק֚וֹל י֣וֹם יְהוָ֔ה מַ֥ר צֹרֵ֖חַ שָׁ֥ם גִּבּֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: Near is the great day of YHWH, near and hastening greatly — the sound of the day of YHWH; the mighty man cries out there bitterly.

notes.official: *qārôḇ yôm-YHWH haggāḏôl* 'Near is the great day of YHWH': the hymn on the day of YHWH (vv14-18) is the source of the medieval sequence *Dies irae*, which takes its opening from the Vulgate of v15. *qôl yôm YHWH mar ṣōrēaḥ šām gibbôr*: the Masoretic accents divide after 'YHWH', giving 'the sound of the day of YHWH; the mighty man cries out there bitterly' (ASV). Emendations join *mar* 'bitter' to the day (NRSV 'the sound of the day of the LORD is bitter') or read *qal* 'swift'. The MT division is kept (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zephaniah-1`; `mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: י֥וֹם עֶבְרָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא י֧וֹם צָרָ֣ה וּמְצוּקָ֗ה י֤וֹם שֹׁאָה֙ וּמְשׁוֹאָ֔ה י֥וֹם חֹ֙שֶׁךְ֙ וַאֲפֵלָ֔ה י֥וֹם עָנָ֖ן וַעֲרָפֶֽל׃

i18n.en: That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of wasteness and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness,

notes.official: *yôm ʿeḇrâ* 'a day of wrath' (Vulgate *dies irae*). *ṣārâ ûməṣûqâ* 'distress and anguish' (central `tzarah-distress-tribulation-vocabulary`); *šōʾâ ûməšôʾâ* 'wasteness and desolation' (ASV), a sound-pair; *ʿānān waʿărāp̄el* 'clouds and thick darkness', the theophany pair of Deut 4:11 and Joel 2:2 (central `arafel-thick-darkness-divine-presence-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: י֥וֹם שׁוֹפָ֖ר וּתְרוּעָ֑ה עַ֚ל הֶעָרִ֣ים הַבְּצֻר֔וֹת וְעַ֖ל הַפִּנּ֥וֹת הַגְּבֹהֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: a day of the shofar and alarm against the fortified cities and against the high battlements.

notes.official: *yôm šôp̄ār ûṯərûʿâ* 'a day of the shofar and alarm': the ram's horn and the war-cry raised against fortified cities (Josh 6:5; Amos 2:2). The line transliterates 'shofar' under the corpus ruling (`shofar-latter-prophets`; Exodus, Kings), replacing the draft's ASV 'trumpet'; isaiah-woh has 'a great trumpet' at Isa 27:13, a divergence flagged for the founder. *happinnôṯ haggəḇōhôṯ* 'the high battlements', the corner towers.

paragraphs.text: וַהֲצֵרֹ֣תִי לָאָדָ֗ם וְהָֽלְכוּ֙ כַּֽעִוְרִ֔ים כִּ֥י לַֽיהוָ֖ה חָטָ֑אוּ וְשֻׁפַּ֤ךְ דָּמָם֙ כֶּֽעָפָ֔ר וּלְחֻמָ֖ם כַּגְּלָלִֽים׃

i18n.en: And I will bring distress upon men, and they shall walk like the blind, because they have sinned against YHWH; and their blood shall be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung.

notes.official: *wahăṣērōṯî lāʾāḏām* 'And I will bring distress upon men': the generic *ʾāḏām* is rendered 'men' (ASV), outside the *ʾāḏām* / *ʾăḏāmâ* pair of vv2-3. *ûləḥumām kaggəlālîm* 'and their flesh like dung': *ləḥûm* is a rare word, 'flesh, bowels' (cf. Job 20:23).

paragraphs.text: גַּם־כַּסְפָּ֨ם גַּם־זְהָבָ֜ם לֹֽא־יוּכַ֣ל לְהַצִּילָ֗ם בְּיוֹם֙ עֶבְרַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וּבְאֵשׁ֙ קִנְאָת֔וֹ תֵּאָכֵ֖ל כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־כָלָ֤ה אַךְ־נִבְהָלָה֙ יַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה אֵ֥ת כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאָֽרֶץ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them on the day of YHWH's wrath; and the whole earth shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy; for he will make an end, yes, a terrible end, of all the inhabitants of the earth.

notes.official: *kol-hāʾāreṣ* 'the whole earth' and *kol-yōšəḇê hāʾāreṣ* 'all the inhabitants of the earth': the chapter's closing frame returns to the universal judgment of vv2-3, and the same phrase recurs at 3:8 in a judgment on all nations, so *ʾereṣ* is rendered in its universal scope (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`; NRSV 'earth'). The draft's 'land' followed the ASV and NJPS, which read the verse of Judah. *bəʾēš qinʾāṯô* 'by the fire of his jealousy' (Deut 4:24). *kālâ ʾaḵ-nibhālâ* 'an end, yes, a terrible end' (ASV 'a full end, yea, a terrible end').
